description: Every [PATH-X] and [PATH-X-Y] tagged decision node, extracted from its source file. Each node keeps its original ID so a chosen pattern traces back to source. `node_type: "top_level_pattern"`/`"sub_decision"` nodes are per-template decision-tree branches (settings-pages.md, table-list.md, forms.md, dialogs-and-action-sheets.md, detail-pages.md). `node_type: "cross_cutting_rule"` nodes are binary, checkable rules from permissions-and-conditional-logic.md that apply across templates rather than belonging to one decision tree — `parent` is `null` for these, same as a top-level pattern, since they don't nest under a single PATH. The remaining untagged worked examples and righter-routing call-outs stay in the reference .md files. microcopy-routing.md carries no PATH- tags (it's a routing checklist to the righter skill, not a testable requirement) and is not represented here. pricing-pages.md adds PATH-F (top-level) with PATH-F-* sub-decisions, plus PATH-PRICE-* cross_cutting_rule nodes (U universal, T tier count, S seat, X usage, H hybrid, C consumer). table-interactions.md adds PATH-TABLE-* cross_cutting_rule nodes (selection and bulk, toolbar and view state, editing and saving, loading, empty and error states, structure). table-list.md also carries the PATH-B-SIMPLE, PATH-B-COMPLEX, PATH-B-ROW-OPEN, and PATH-B-EDIT sub_decision nodes.

nodes.condition: User is managing profile, workspace, team, billing, notifications, or members. Multiple related sections that don't need to be edited simultaneously. Changes persist immediately or on explicit save.
nodes.outcome: Use the Settings Page pattern. Depth (shallow vs. deep) is decided by PATH-A-DEPTH-SHALLOW / PATH-A-DEPTH-DEEP. Mobile: sidebar becomes a hamburger menu that slides out and overlaps content.

nodes.condition: 2-3 sections only.
nodes.outcome: Horizontal tabs pinned to top (single page). Structure: page title + tabs + tab content area.

nodes.condition: 4+ sections.
nodes.outcome: Sidebar navigation + sub-pages. Structure: sidebar (pinned on desktop, hamburger on mobile) + main content area.

nodes.condition: User needs to browse, search, filter, and act on multiple items. User occasionally dives into single item details. Bulk actions might be needed.
nodes.outcome: Use the Table/List with Details pattern. Decide simple or complex (PATH-B-SIMPLE, PATH-B-COMPLEX), then how a row opens (PATH-B-ROW-OPEN) and where editing happens (PATH-B-EDIT). Row detail: a drawer by default, with an Open action that escalates to a full page when the record has tabs, a timeline, related records, or a long form. Behavior inside the table is covered by the PATH-TABLE-* rules.

nodes.condition: User is creating a new item, editing an existing item, or completing a workflow/multi-step process.
nodes.outcome: Use the Form pattern. Complexity (simple/medium/complex) is decided by field count via PATH-C-SIMPLE / PATH-C-MEDIUM / PATH-C-COMPLEX.

nodes.condition: 1-6 fields (simple form).
nodes.outcome: Single column, stack vertically. No grouping needed. Space between fields: the 24px scale step (`gap-6` in Tailwind).

nodes.condition: 7-15 fields (medium form).
nodes.outcome: Single column OR 2 columns. Group related inputs with section headers (e.g. an address group: street, city, state, zip). Space within a section: the 24px scale step (`gap-6`) between fields, the 40px step (`gap-10`) between sections.

nodes.condition: 15+ fields OR complex relationships.
nodes.outcome: Tabs OR 2 columns with sections. Group related fields under section headers (e.g. event creation: left = basic info, right = advanced settings).

nodes.condition: Single quick input needed (amount, selection, confirmation). Simple confirmation (yes/no, approve/reject). Dropdown selection, especially on mobile.
nodes.outcome: Desktop: modal dialog, centered, backdrop dims content behind. Mobile: action sheet, slides up from bottom, covers 80-90% screen height for multi-step. Never use an action sheet if text input/keyboard is required — that needs a full modal. Footer button placement: primary right, secondary the 20px scale step (`gap-5`) left of primary, optional tertiary on the left.

nodes.condition: User is viewing a single record in read-only mode. No editing at this level (editing happens on a dedicated form page). User might click through to edit on a separate page.
nodes.outcome: Header: breadcrumb above H1 title, close/back button top right if in a modal. Body: groups of related data stacked vertically, each group as label + value, status indicators/badges where relevant. Actions: no primary action in view-only state; an "Edit" link/button navigates to the form page if editing is available. Mobile: stacked single column, no horizontal grouping.

nodes.rule_name: Hide Page Elements by Role
nodes.condition: User role doesn't have permission to see an element (e.g. non-admin viewing a Members section, non-owner viewing Billing, unpermitted user viewing a Delete account button).
nodes.outcome: Hide the element entirely — it never renders in the DOM. This is deletion, not disabling. Check role at render time; don't render the element at all.

nodes.rule_name: Disable Controls by Permission or Condition
nodes.condition: Content the user cannot update due to an org admin setting or a cascading choice condition (e.g. a workspace admin disabled this setting, the record is archived).
nodes.outcome: Keep the element visible but disabled, in a view-only/disabled state, so the user can visually map the cause/effect relationship. Route the disabled-state explanation (tooltip or helper text) to righter skill.

nodes.rule_name: Mask personal data by default
nodes.condition: A list, table, card, or header shows personal data (email, phone, street address, date of birth, government ID, payment number) to a user whose task doesn't need the full value.
nodes.outcome: Show a masked value by default: `j***@acme.com`, `•••• 4821`, last four digits only. A person's name stays visible on a screen whose job is that person (a people list, a profile). Show the full value only to roles that need it, and only through the reveal control (`PATH-PERM-PII-REVEAL`) or on a detail view. A role that never needs it never receives it. Mask on the server, so the full value never reaches the page for roles that can't see it. CSS blur or hiding is not masking. Masked values keep the column width so the layout doesn't jump.
nodes.basis_note: judgment. Drafted at Om's request on 2026-10-06. The decision to add PII rules is confirmed. The rule wording has not been reviewed, and no Mobbin evidence was checked.

nodes.rule_name: Reveal a masked value on request
nodes.condition: A role that is allowed to see a masked value needs the full one.
nodes.outcome: Put a reveal control on that one field, not on the whole page, and wherever the masked value appears (a list row, a card, a header, or a detail view): an icon Button with a label such as "Show email". The value re-masks when the user leaves the view or after a timeout. Log reveals of high-risk fields (government ID, payment, health data) on the server. Copy to clipboard copies the full value only for roles that may reveal it.
nodes.basis_note: judgment. Drafted at Om's request on 2026-10-06. The decision to add PII rules is confirmed. The rule wording has not been reviewed, and no Mobbin evidence was checked.

nodes.rule_name: Keep personal data out of URLs, titles, file names, and analytics
nodes.condition: Building a URL, query string, page title, breadcrumb, browser history entry, export file name, or analytics event for a screen that involves a person.
nodes.outcome: Use opaque IDs, not personal data: `/customers/c_8f2a`, not `/customers/jane.doe@acme.com`. A title or breadcrumb may show a name only on a screen whose job is that person, and never an email, phone number, address, or ID. Name exports by content and date, such as `customers-2026-10-06.csv`. Analytics properties carry IDs, never values (see `metrics-tagging`). For error, toast, and notification copy, see righter `no-pii-in-copy`.
nodes.basis_note: judgment. Drafted at Om's request on 2026-10-06. The decision to add PII rules is confirmed. The rule wording has not been reviewed, and no Mobbin evidence was checked.

nodes.rule_name: Parent/Child Input Dependencies
nodes.condition: A group of related inputs has a conditional relationship — a child input's valid options or availability depend on a parent input's value.
nodes.outcome: Disable the affected child inputs until the parent input is updated/selected with a valid value. Show them disabled but visible, not hidden, so the relationship stays legible. Route the explanation to righter skill.

nodes.rule_name: Primary Button State
nodes.condition: A form has a primary submit action gated on required fields.
nodes.outcome: The primary button is disabled until all required fields have been filled with valid responses. Route the disabled-state tooltip (e.g. "Fill in all required fields to continue") to righter skill.

nodes.rule_name: Cascading Accordion/Expansion
nodes.condition: A layout contains multiple expandable/accordion forms.
nodes.outcome: Only one form can remain expanded at a time. Auto-collapse the previously expanded one when the user opens a new one.

nodes.rule_name: Simple Calculation Tables
nodes.condition: A calculation dynamically updates a final value from inline input fields and dropdowns (e.g. quantity × unit price).
nodes.outcome: Use a simple table layout: header row acts as the field label, inline inputs and dropdowns, and never stack more than 4 rows.

nodes.rule_name: Check for a Direct Fit First
nodes.condition: A feature brief names its own product-specific job (e.g. "approval queue", "impersonate a user") rather than one of the five container types.
nodes.outcome: Translate the brief into a plain job-to-be-done and re-check it against the SKILL.md decision tree before assuming it needs new structure. Most briefs that sound novel because of their product-specific name are a direct fit for an existing path once translated.

nodes.rule_name: Combine Existing Patterns Before Inventing a Third
nodes.condition: A brief needs more than one container type's job done at once (e.g. browse-and-approve, multi-step form with a review step, bulk edit from a list).
nodes.outcome: Compose the existing container types that each cover part of the job (e.g. PATH-B + PATH-D for an approval queue; PATH-C + PATH-E for a form with a review step) instead of designing one bespoke hybrid container. If you can't name which existing pattern is doing each part of the job, that's the signal to check PATH-COMPOSITION-INVENT-LAST instead.

nodes.rule_name: Invent New Structure Only As a Last Resort, and Say So
nodes.condition: The job doesn't fit any existing container type directly (PATH-COMPOSITION-CHECK-FIRST) or as a composition of existing ones (PATH-COMPOSITION-COMBINE).
nodes.outcome: Build new structure, but name which existing patterns were considered and why they didn't fit — the same reasoning vois_report_pattern_gap asks for, called if available, stated in your own output if not. A new pattern invented this way is a one-off for the brief in front of you, not automatically a new entry in this skill; promoting it to a sixth container type requires the same deliberate review (SKILL.md + patterns-rules.json) every existing path already had.

nodes.rule_name: Dense Layout
nodes.condition: Power user or admin doing this repeatedly; scanning or comparing many rows at once; screen real estate at a premium relative to how much needs to be visible (admin data grids, financial/analytics tables, dashboards, log/audit views).
nodes.outcome: Lean toward the tighter end of the spacing scale (--space-4/-8/-12 between related items), more columns/metrics visible without scrolling, smaller non-body type sizes where DS-TYPOGRAPHY still allows it.

nodes.rule_name: Standard Layout
nodes.condition: Default for most product surfaces — forms, settings pages, typical list/detail views — when neither PATH-DENSITY-DENSE nor PATH-DENSITY-SPACIOUS's conditions apply.
nodes.outcome: Lean toward the mid spacing scale (--space-16/-24), the values forms.md and settings-pages.md already specify. This is the correct default absent a specific reason to use dense or spacious.

nodes.rule_name: Spacious Layout
nodes.condition: Low-frequency, high-stakes, or attention-focusing moment — onboarding/first-run, empty states, a destructive-confirmation dialog, marketing/landing surfaces, a single critical rarely-seen decision point.
nodes.outcome: Lean toward the looser end of the spacing scale (--space-32/-48 and up), fewer things visible at once, more whitespace around the one thing that matters. Optimize for making one decision unmistakable, not for efficiency.

nodes.condition: User is showing what a product costs and helping a buyer choose a plan. Billing unit is flat, seat-based, usage-based, hybrid, or consumer subscription, with 1 to 4 real tiers.
nodes.outcome: Use the Pricing Page pattern. Billing model picks the sub-decision (PATH-F-FLAT-1 through PATH-F-CONSUMER-PAYWALL). Universal rules (PATH-PRICE-U*) apply to every pricing page. Tier-count rules (PATH-PRICE-T*) apply to layout. Model-specific rules (S, X, H, C) apply per sub-decision.

nodes.condition: Flat price, one plan (no seats, no meter).
nodes.outcome: Single centered card: price with unit and period, 4 to 8 numeric features, one CTA. See PATH-PRICE-T1. Add a small secondary path for large buyers.

nodes.condition: Seat-based, one plan.
nodes.outcome: Single card with per-seat price, included seats, and a seat quantity control (minus and plus around a number) or an input if count changes the price. See PATH-PRICE-T1, PATH-PRICE-S1 to S5.

nodes.condition: Seat-based, 2 to 3 plans.
nodes.outcome: Cards side by side, highlight the middle (or the paid tier when there are 2). Per-seat price with period, included seats, caps disclosed. See PATH-PRICE-T2, T3, S1 to S7.

nodes.condition: Seat-based, 4 plans (Free, Pro, Team, Enterprise).
nodes.outcome: Four cards with short bullets plus a comparison table below. Enterprise shows Custom. Define seat types that bill differently. See PATH-PRICE-T4, S4, S6, U11.

nodes.condition: Usage-based, one plan and one rate.
nodes.outcome: Single card plus an estimator: slider with number input, rate table, itemized total labeled estimated. See PATH-PRICE-X1 to X6.

nodes.condition: Usage-based, 2 to 4 plans, each with an included allowance and overage.
nodes.outcome: Plan cards show base price and allowance in the buyer's unit. A calculator below recommends a plan from the input and shows overage separately. See PATH-PRICE-X2, X7, X8.

nodes.condition: Pure pay-as-you-go with no plans.
nodes.outcome: Calculator-first page: slider plus input, live rate table with the active tier highlighted, itemized breakdown, big estimated total, and a note on custom pricing for large volume. See PATH-PRICE-X1 to X5, X10, X11.

nodes.condition: Seat fee plus included usage plus overage.
nodes.outcome: Cards show base price and allowance. A calculator (plan, seats, usage, add-ons, total) shows the real bill with monthly and annual totals. See PATH-PRICE-H1 to H4.

nodes.condition: Consumer subscription on a web page (individual, family, student).
nodes.outcome: Selectable plan cards with a clear selected state and one Continue button. Name family plans by accounts or devices. Show monthly equivalent and real charge. See PATH-PRICE-C1, C2, C6.

nodes.condition: Consumer subscription on iOS or in-app paywall.
nodes.outcome: Plan cards, trial timeline, CTA that agrees with post-trial price, Restore Purchases, Terms, Privacy. Timing and placement route to conversion-patterns. See PATH-PRICE-C2 to C5, C8, C11.

nodes.rule_name: One lockup for price
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: Show price, unit, and billing period together: "$24 per person / month, billed annually." Seen on Descript, Height, Plain. Never split the unit into a footnote.

nodes.rule_name: Annual toggle states its savings
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: "Save 25%," "2 months free," "-20%." Put it next to the toggle, not in a tooltip. Every price on the page must change when the toggle flips. Default to annual only if annual is what you want to sell.

nodes.rule_name: Show the annual total when annual is on
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: Copy.ai and Kit both show "$36/mo, billed $432/year." Buyers do the math anyway. Do it for them.

nodes.rule_name: One highlighted tier, never two
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: Use a border or elevation plus a short badge ("Most popular," "Recommended"). Do not rely on color alone.

nodes.rule_name: Only the highlighted tier gets the primary button
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: Others get secondary style. Descript and Plain do this well. Teachable colors one and blacks the others, which is close but inconsistent when the highlight and the button color disagree.

nodes.rule_name: CTA matches the friction
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: Free: "Start free." Paid with trial: "Start free trial." Top tier: "Talk to sales." Do not put "Get started" on every card.

nodes.rule_name: Use "Everything in X, plus:"
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: on every tier above the first. Dub, Height, Windsurf, Circle all do it. It cuts repeated bullets and shows the ladder.

nodes.rule_name: Limits are numbers, not adjectives
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: "30 transcription hours / month" beats "generous limits." Keep to about 6 to 8 bullets per card. If a card runs longer, the extra goes in the comparison table.

nodes.rule_name: "No credit card required" near the free or trial CTA, only when true
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: Seen on Dub, Clay, Lyssna.

nodes.rule_name: Enterprise says "Custom" in the price slot
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: List what sales unlocks (SSO, audit logs, dedicated support). Don't invent a starting price you won't honor.

nodes.rule_name: Define any term that changes the bill
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: Retool footnotes "standard users" vs "end users." If two things look like seats but bill differently, define both below the cards.

nodes.rule_name: State tax and currency
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: Mistral says "excluding taxes" and has a currency switch. Do this if you sell across regions.

nodes.rule_name: Below the cards, in this order:
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: comparison table (3+ tiers), FAQ, reassurance line (cancel anytime, money-back). *Design judgment, not one observed order.*

nodes.rule_name: Mobile stacks cards with the recommended tier first
nodes.condition: Any pricing page, regardless of billing model or tier count.
nodes.outcome: *Design judgment.* Users won't scroll past three tall cards to find the one you want them to see.

nodes.rule_name: One tier
nodes.condition: Deciding how many tiers to show and how to lay them out.
nodes.outcome: One card, centered, price, 4 to 8 features, one CTA. Reflect ("One plan one price") and Skillshare do this. If price varies by a size variable, put the control inside the card (Kit's subscriber dropdown). Add a small secondary path for big buyers ("Request a demo").

nodes.rule_name: Two tiers
nodes.condition: Deciding how many tiers to show and how to lay them out.
nodes.outcome: Works best when the split is "me vs us" (Personal / Team) or "free vs paid." Highlight the paid one.

nodes.rule_name: Three tiers
nodes.condition: Deciding how many tiers to show and how to lay them out.
nodes.outcome: The default. Name tiers by audience or stage, not Good/Better/Best. Seen: Hobbyist / Creator / Business (Descript), Launch / Grow / Scale (Plain), Starter / Pro / Enterprise (Current).

nodes.rule_name: Four tiers
nodes.condition: Deciding how many tiers to show and how to lay them out.
nodes.outcome: Windsurf, Mistral, Retool, and Firecrawl show four. Only do it when the fourth is a real sales-led tier. Keep card bullets short and put depth in a comparison table. Airtable and Lyssna both use a sticky-header table with grouped sections.

nodes.rule_name: Five or more
nodes.condition: Deciding how many tiers to show and how to lay them out.
nodes.outcome: Only for consumer products with distinct benefit stories. Revolut uses five cards with short descriptions and arrows. Klarna uses tabs plus cards. Never a five-column row of feature bullets.

nodes.rule_name: Price per seat per month, with the period
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).
nodes.outcome: Plain: "$39 / user / month." Say who counts as a seat.

nodes.rule_name: Show included seats
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).
nodes.outcome: Copy.ai: "5 user seats included." Lyssna shows both "included seats" and "maximum seats" per tier.

nodes.rule_name: Add a quantity control on the card when seat count changes the price
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).
nodes.outcome: Mistral puts "$50/mo, 2 users" with +/- on the Team card. GitBook uses a number input and shows a running total. Show monthly and annual totals.

nodes.rule_name: Separate seat types and say so
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).
nodes.outcome: Lyssna has viewer seats. Retool has standard users and end users with different prices. If you have free viewers or cheaper light users, show that as a feature, not fine print.

nodes.rule_name: Disclose caps
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).
nodes.outcome: "Up to 50 members" (Height), "max 15 seats" (Lyssna). Buyers hit these walls later and feel tricked if you hid them.

nodes.rule_name: Volume discounts live on the Enterprise card
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).
nodes.outcome: Windsurf: "Volume based annual discounts (>200 seats)."

nodes.rule_name: If the free tier has unlimited seats, say it loudly
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with seats (per-user, per-member).
nodes.outcome: Height and Current lead with "unlimited members." It's a differentiator.

nodes.rule_name: Never show only a per-unit rate
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: A rate like "1.8 cents per charge" is meaningless without a sample bill. Add an estimator (Stripe, Vercel, Cofounder).

nodes.rule_name: Ask in the customer's unit
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Kit asks "How many email subscribers do you have?" Teak asks "Avg. daily active players." Cartesia converts credits to minutes of audio. If your billing unit is abstract (tokens, credits, blocks), translate it. Mailchimp's "blocks of 25,000 emails" is the version to avoid.

nodes.rule_name: Slider plus number input
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Vercel and Grok pair them. The slider is for exploring, the input is for exactness. Label the tick marks.

nodes.rule_name: Show the rate table next to the calculator
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Stripe highlights the active tier under the slider track. Mailchimp shows the full block-rate table. Buyers want to verify your math.

nodes.rule_name: Big estimated total, plus an itemized breakdown
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Cofounder lists token, compute, and database costs above a large total. Vercel does the same and adds a comparison. Always label it "estimated."

nodes.rule_name: Default to a realistic value, not zero
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Cartesia starts at 45 min. Mailchimp's empty state shows $0.00, which tells the buyer nothing. *My read, not tested.*

nodes.rule_name: Show included allowance and overage separately
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Cofounder: "$20 included." Windsurf: "Add-on credits at $10 / 250 credits." Say what happens when they run out.

nodes.rule_name: Recommend a plan from the input
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Cartesia shows a "Recommended plan" card after you pick volume. Kit disables tiers that can't cover your count ("Max subscribers reached").

nodes.rule_name: Say what one unit buys
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: If you sell credits, give an example ("1 credit = about 2 pages scraped"). ClassPass explains credits in its own page and notes rollover. Rollover is worth stating.

nodes.rule_name: Offer a reset on multi-input calculators
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Grok has one.

nodes.rule_name: Predictability is a feature
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: If you don't meter something, show it as $0. Agentcard lists "$0 per issued card" and "$0 per order" under a flat monthly fee. If you have a spending cap or pause, say so.

nodes.rule_name: Outcome pricing needs a definition
nodes.condition: Pricing that scales with usage (volume, credits, tokens, events).
nodes.outcome: Intercom prices Fin at "$0.99 per outcome." Any outcome-based price must define what counts as one, on the same screen.

nodes.rule_name: Show usage per seat
nodes.condition: Pricing that combines a seat fee with included usage and overage.
nodes.outcome: Windsurf: "500 prompt credits / user / month." Buyers multiply by team size. Put the multiplication in the calculator.

nodes.rule_name: Calculator order follows how buyers think
nodes.condition: Pricing that combines a seat fee with included usage and overage.
nodes.outcome: Plan, then seats, then usage, then add-ons, then total. GitBook: plan, site count, users, total per month and per year. Teak adds an add-on toggle.

nodes.rule_name: Two totals
nodes.condition: Pricing that combines a seat fee with included usage and overage.
nodes.outcome: Monthly and annual, always.

nodes.rule_name: Keep the cards simple, put the math in the calculator
nodes.condition: Pricing that combines a seat fee with included usage and overage.
nodes.outcome: Cards show the base price and allowance. The calculator shows the real bill. Don't cram both into one card.

nodes.rule_name: Plan choice is radio cards with one Continue button
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: MasterClass and Quizlet show cards with a clear selected state and one button below. Do not hide prices behind a tap.

nodes.rule_name: Show both the monthly equivalent and the real charge
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Blue Apron: "$8.33/mo" plus "$99.99/yr." Lifesum shows per-month next to the billing period. Yubo's "$0.60/day" is fine only if the actual charge is also visible.

nodes.rule_name: Explain the trial as a timeline
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Quizlet: today (access), reminder date, trial ends, billing starts. Jomo says "We'll notify you 24h before your trial ends." This is the single clearest trust builder in the set.

nodes.rule_name: The CTA and the small print agree
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: "Start free trial" with "7-day free, then $29.98/year" right under it (Halide). Blue Apron adds a terms checkbox before enabling the button.

nodes.rule_name: iOS: always show Restore Purchases, Terms, Privacy
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Jomo, Lifesum, Notion all do.

nodes.rule_name: Name family plans by who's in them
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Deezer: "1 account / 2 accounts / 6 accounts." MasterClass: "1 account, 6 devices."

nodes.rule_name: Free vs Pro list when free is real
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Tide Guide shows a checklist with two columns. It makes the upgrade feel concrete.

nodes.rule_name: Sticky CTAs must not cover a plan
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Tide Guide's button sits over the annual plan card in the screen I saw. Test with the smallest supported device.

nodes.rule_name: Strikethrough anchors only for real prior prices
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Lifesum and Deezer use them. If the higher price was never charged, don't show it. *Ethical rule, not observed.*

nodes.rule_name: One line on why it costs money
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Halide has a "Why is Halide not free?" block. For indie or small-team apps it earns trust.

nodes.rule_name: Placement, timing, and trial-vs-no-trial go to `conversion-patterns`
nodes.condition: Consumer subscription pricing (individual, family, student) on web or iOS.
nodes.outcome: Placement, timing, and trial-vs-no-trial go to `conversion-patterns`.

nodes.condition: The user changes a Switch, Select, or Radio that stands alone on a settings page.
nodes.outcome: Persist on change and confirm with a toast. If the save fails, revert the control and surface the failure with whichever component righter's decision tree picks. No Save button.

nodes.pattern_name: Explicit save for text and multi-field blocks
nodes.condition: A settings block has text inputs or more than one related field.
nodes.outcome: Save stays disabled until a value has changed and every required value is valid. Cancel restores the last saved values. Both sit in the block, not in a footer.

nodes.pattern_name: Where the view state still applies
nodes.condition: A settings block holds details that are mostly read and rarely changed, such as legal name, business address, or billing details.
nodes.outcome: Use the view state by default and enter the edit state on an explicit Edit action, as `settings-pages.md` describes. Preference blocks are always editable and skip the view state.
nodes.basis_note: decision. Confirmed by Om. Reconciles the existing view-then-edit model with the always-editable pages most products ship.

nodes.condition: Laying out preference rows, each with a label and one control.
nodes.outcome: Label and optional helper text (Description style) on the left, control on the right, centered vertically. Group header above the rows. Rows separated by dividers. No container card or shadow around a group. Cap the content column at `--width-form-max` and space groups with `gap-10`. When the container is narrower than the `sm` value (`40em`), stack the control under its label.
nodes.basis_note: observed layout. Linear wraps its rows in a bordered container, but DS-SLOP-010 discourages card-ifying static groups, so the container is dropped. Column cap and stacking are judgment.

nodes.condition: There are two or more channels and three or more event types.
nodes.outcome: Events are rows and channels are columns, grouped under category headers. Each cell is a Switch when changes save instantly, or a Checkbox only when the page has an explicit Save. With one channel, use a plain list of Switches. Below the `sm` container width, each event stacks with its channels listed beneath it.
nodes.basis_note: observed matrix. Most products pair checkboxes with instant save, which JOB-BINARY-PREFERENCE does not allow, so the component follows Vois. Mobile collapse is judgment.

nodes.condition: A channel column exists but the channel is not connected, for example Slack.
nodes.outcome: Keep the column visible and disabled, with a link to connect it.

nodes.condition: The product sends a digest email.
nodes.outcome: Put its Switch above the matrix as its own row, separate from the per-event preferences.

nodes.condition: Listing members of a workspace or team.
nodes.outcome: Columns are member (name and email), role, and status. Row actions follow `[PATH-B-ROW-ACTIONS]`, so Remove and other secondary actions sit in the DropdownMenu. The Invite primary button sits at the top right of the table. Narrow layout follows `[PATH-B-NARROW]`.

nodes.condition: The user adds a member.
nodes.outcome: The Invite button opens a Dialog with email and role. Use an inline email field with an Invite button only when inviting is the main job of the page. The toast names the invited address.
nodes.basis_note: observed for both forms. The choice between them is judgment.

nodes.condition: A member row is pending or active.
nodes.outcome: Pending rows get a Pending badge and the menu actions Resend invite and Remove. Active rows get Edit role and Remove. When the role list is short, role can be an inline Select that saves instantly.
nodes.basis_note: observed. Inline versus menu is judgment.

nodes.condition: A member row is the current user or the owner.
nodes.outcome: Label the current user's row "You". The owner row has no Remove. The current user's action is Leave, not Remove. Removing someone else uses an AlertDialog and notifies the removed member afterward.

nodes.condition: Listing integrations.
nodes.outcome: Show Connected above Available, each with a count. Rows are a list by default. Use a card grid only when browsing a large catalog, and add search and a category filter there.

nodes.condition: Choosing row actions for an integration.
nodes.outcome: Not connected: Connect. Connected: Configure when there are settings, plus a quiet Disconnect. Disconnect is never the primary button and is red only if it deletes data. A Connect that leaves the app shows an external-link icon.

nodes.condition: An integration needs a higher plan.
nodes.outcome: Show it disabled with the plan requirement stated. Do not hide it. This differs from role-denied items, which are hidden.
nodes.basis_note: observed. The hide-versus-show distinction is judgment.

nodes.condition: The deletion is irreversible or high-impact, such as a workspace, team, or account.
nodes.outcome: The user types the object's name before the destructive button enables. The body lists what will be lost with counts and states any recovery window. It always uses a full modal, never an action sheet. Dialog width follows `[PATH-D-SIZE]`, which is the small tier.

nodes.condition: A page has account-, workspace-, or team-level destructive actions.
nodes.outcome: Group them at the bottom under a Danger zone heading. Each row has a label and helper text on the left and a destructive button on the right. Leave and delete are separate rows.

nodes.condition: Showing a sign-in identifier such as email.
nodes.outcome: Show it read-only with an explicit Edit control and a Verified badge when verified. Edit starts `[PATH-SET-EMAIL-CHANGE]`. Never a plain input with a Save button.

nodes.condition: The user chooses to change their email.
nodes.outcome: A full page at its own route, not a dialog. Two steps shown with a Stepper. Step 1 is the new address, plus the current password when the session is not recent. Step 2 is the code. Follow `JOB-NAVIGATION-POSITION` for the Breadcrumb or Back link, and cap the form container at `--width-form-max`. Step 1 buttons are Cancel (returns to settings, address unchanged) and Next. Step 2 buttons are Back (returns to step 1 with the typed address kept) and Verify. Each step validates before the next. No retype-to-confirm field, since the code already proves the address works.
nodes.basis_note: decision. Om chose a full page so the flow can use a Stepper, which `JOB-MULTISTEP-GUIDE` requires for 2 to 5 steps. Most products reviewed use a dialog (Discord flow, Monarch flow, Adobe flow), and AWS flow uses a full page. Re-auth is seen in Discord and AWS, and the session-recency condition is judgment.

nodes.condition: Step 2 of the email change.
nodes.outcome: Send the code to the new address. The current address stays active until the code verifies. The body names the exact address and offers a way back to correct it. State the code length, and state the expiry when the code expires. After a successful change, notify the previous address.
nodes.basis_note: observed for sending to the new address (AWS flow), naming it, offering to change it (Posh, Eventbrite, Walmart, ManyChat, Pipedrive), stating length (Monarch flow, Pipedrive), and stating expiry (Hulu, GoFundMe). Notifying the old address is judgment.

nodes.condition: The user enters the code.
nodes.outcome: A primary Verify button in the step footer, replacing Next, disabled until every cell is filled. Back is the secondary. While verifying, show an inline Spinner in the button. Do not submit automatically on the last digit.
nodes.basis_note: observed button pattern (Monarch flow, Clerk, Wix, Hulu). No auto-submit is judgment.

nodes.condition: The user did not receive the code.
nodes.outcome: A text link under the field. After each send, disable it and show the remaining wait in or beside it. Do not hide it. The wait length is a product setting, not a Vois value. A resend clears the cells, because the old code stops working, and confirms with a toast.

nodes.condition: The code is wrong or has expired.
nodes.outcome: Show the error inline directly under the field with righter's Helper Text, using an icon plus text, and put every cell in the error state. Keep the digits, selected so typing replaces them. Never a toast for this. An expired code also brings the Resend link into focus. Copy and component choice come from righter.
nodes.basis_note: observed inline (Databricks, Copy.ai, Clerk, GoFundMe, Walmart). Toast errors (Uvodo code, Posh) lose to JOB-TRANSIENT-FEEDBACK. Selecting the kept digits is judgment.

nodes.condition: The code verifies.
nodes.outcome: Return to the settings page, show the new address in the row with the Verified badge, and confirm with a toast. Until then the row keeps showing the old address.

nodes.condition: Building any form.
nodes.outcome: Cap the form container at `--width-form-max`. The layout holds down to `--width-viewport-min` with no horizontal scroll.

nodes.condition: Sizing a field.
nodes.outcome: Single-line inputs and selects fill their column up to `--width-field-max`. Short fixed-format values (postal code, state or province code, expiry, security code) cap at `--width-field-narrow` and never stretch. Multi-line textareas may fill up to `--width-form-max` and grow in height per `[PATH-FIELD-TEXTAREA-AUTOSIZE]`. Single-line fields never exceed `--width-field-max`.

nodes.condition: Placing fields side by side.
nodes.outcome: Use at most two columns. Pair only related fields of similar length, such as first and last name, or state and postal code. Address line 1, email, phone, and textareas always sit alone. Dialogs are always one column (`[PATH-D-SIZE]`). Visual order equals tab order.
nodes.basis_note: decision for the limit and for no columns in dialogs. The pairings are observed.

nodes.condition: The form's container gets narrow.
nodes.outcome: Two columns become one when the form's container is narrower than the `sm` breakpoint value (`40em`). Use a container query so forms inside drawers and side panels wrap correctly. Source order is preserved. The phone control and the one-time-code group never split.
nodes.basis_note: decision for the wrap. The container-query choice follows the existing Vois rule.

nodes.condition: Two columns sit side by side.
nodes.outcome: `gap-6` by default and `gap-10` when the DENSITY dial is 3 or lower. Vertical gaps between fields and sections are already set in `forms.md` (`gap-6` and `gap-10`).
nodes.basis_note: decision. The 24 to 40 range and the link to the DENSITY dial are both confirmed by Om.

nodes.condition: Marking which fields are required.
nodes.outcome: If most fields are required, mark the optional ones "(optional)" instead of marking every required one. Label placement and style are already covered.

nodes.condition: Collecting a person's name.
nodes.outcome: First name and last name as a pair. Use one full-name field only when the product treats the name as a single string.

nodes.condition: Building an address form.
nodes.outcome: Country, address line 1, address line 2, city, then state or province and postal code as a pair. Country goes first because it decides which fields appear and how they are labelled. Changing country re-labels and re-validates without clearing typed values. In settings, line 2 is a visible optional field. In short flows it may collapse behind an "Add apartment, suite" link.

nodes.condition: Placing the lower address fields.
nodes.outcome: State or province at default width pairs with postal code at `--width-field-narrow`. City sits alone. Never put three fields in one row. Set `autocomplete` on every field (address-line1, address-line2, address-level2, address-level1, postal-code, country).
nodes.basis_note: observed for the pairs. Autocomplete values are judgment.

nodes.condition: Collecting a phone number.
nodes.outcome: One joined control with a country selector and a number input on a single row sharing one label. The selector is a Combobox with a fixed width of `w-24` and the number input takes the rest. The row stays on one line at `--width-viewport-min`. The whole control caps at `--width-field-max`. Closed, the selector shows the flag and dial code, and the open list shows country name and dial code with frequently used countries pinned first. The default follows the user's locale.

nodes.condition: The user types a phone number.
nodes.outcome: Format as they type using the selected country's pattern, show a telephone keypad on mobile, and store in international format.
nodes.basis_note: observed for live formatting (Coinbase phone). Keypad and storage format are judgment.

nodes.condition: An email field appears in a regular form.
nodes.outcome: Default width, email keypad and `autocomplete="email"` on mobile. In account settings it follows `[PATH-SET-IDENTITY-FIELD]` instead.

nodes.condition: A multi-line text field, such as notes, a description, or feedback.
nodes.outcome: It grows with its content using CSS `field-sizing: content`, never JavaScript. It starts at `--textarea-min-lines`, stops growing at `--textarea-max-lines`, and scrolls inside after that. The CSS pattern, the required width setting, and the fallback are in `[DS-LAYOUT-FIELD-001]` to `[DS-LAYOUT-FIELD-004]`.
nodes.basis_note: decision. Om specified `field-sizing: content`. Om confirmed the line counts: form textarea 3 to 12, chat input 1 to 8.

nodes.condition: The user types a message into an AI or chat thread.
nodes.outcome: One textarea using the same auto-growing pattern. It starts at `--chat-input-min-lines`, grows to `--chat-input-max-lines`, then scrolls inside. The composer is anchored to the bottom of the thread, so growth pushes upward and the send control stays aligned to the composer's bottom edge. It fills its container and is not capped by `--width-field-max` or `--width-form-max`, because the thread column sets its width. The chat container uses `dvh` so it tracks the mobile keyboard. Keep an accessible name even when there is no visible label.
nodes.basis_note: decision for the autosizing. Judgment for the bottom anchoring, the send-control alignment, and the width exemption. Chat input patterns beyond sizing were not researched.

nodes.condition: The user enters a fixed-length code, such as an email or SMS verification code.
nodes.outcome: Use InputOTP with one cell per character, behaving as one field: one tab stop, paste fills every cell, backspace moves back, `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, and a numeric keypad when the code is digits only. Keep a visible label. Cells share the row equally with `gap-2`, cap at `size-12`, and shrink to fit down to `--width-viewport-min`. The group caps at `--width-field-max`. The group is one hit area of at least `--hit-area-min` tall, and a tap on any cell focuses the first empty one, so cells can shrink visually without losing the target. The error state puts an icon and text under the group and puts every cell in the error style.
nodes.basis_note: observed. 14 of the 18 verification screens reviewed use segmented cells. The rest use one plain field (Monarch flow, Wix, Eventbrite, Discord flow). Segmented seen in Pipedrive, Coinbase code, Hulu, Shopify, Apple Music, Databricks, Clerk. Behavior details and the group-as-one-hit-area approach are judgment.

nodes.condition: Choosing the width of a desktop Dialog or AlertDialog.
nodes.outcome: Two tiers, both maximums, and every dialog is a single column. Small (--width-dialog-sm): confirmations, AlertDialogs, typed confirmation, and dialogs with one or a few stacked fields. Large (--width-dialog-lg): dialogs whose content needs the extra width, such as a textarea or a short list. Two-column layouts go on pages, not in dialogs. On mobile, text-input dialogs are full modals and the tiers do not apply.
nodes.basis_note: Set and confirmed by Om: two tiers and widths, tier chosen by layout need, no two-column layouts in dialogs.

nodes.condition: A table or list row has quick actions.
nodes.outcome: Two visible actions is preferred and three is the maximum. Everything beyond that, including secondary and destructive actions, goes in a DropdownMenu.
nodes.basis_note: Set by Om. Resolves the conflict between table-list.md (max 3) and JOB-EXPOSE-ACTIONS (1 to 2).

nodes.condition: A row's quick actions are revealed on hover.
nodes.outcome: Reveal on hover only where the device supports hover. On touch devices the actions are always visible.
nodes.basis_note: Set by Om. Fixes hover-only actions being unreachable on touch.

nodes.condition: A table's container is narrower than the sm breakpoint value (40em).
nodes.outcome: If the table has 4 or fewer columns, not counting the actions column, rows stack as list items. If it has more, the table scrolls horizontally with the first column and header row pinned.
nodes.basis_note: Set by Om. The 4-column cutoff is Claude's proposal, accepted by Om. Not counting the actions column is Claude's interpretation.

nodes.condition: 6 or fewer columns, mostly read, no bulk actions, no inline edit, one or two filter dimensions.
nodes.outcome: Fixed columns. Search, one filter, and sort. 25 per page. Vertical scroll only: the page scrolls and the header sticks to the page, with no sideways scroll. One density.
nodes.basis_note: judgment. The 6-column cutoff is Claude's proposal.

nodes.condition: More than 6 columns, user-chosen columns or saved views, bulk actions, inline edit, many filter dimensions, or thousands of rows.
nodes.outcome: Toolbar with search, filter builder, columns, density, and saved views. Checkbox column and bulk bar. The table wrapper owns scroll on both axes with a bounded height, header and first column pinned, scroll locked to one axis per gesture. Dense, Regular, and Comfortable densities.
nodes.basis_note: decision. Set by Om: gesture lock for complex tables, vertical-only for simple ones, density toggle on complex tables only.

nodes.condition: A user opens a row to see its record.
nodes.outcome: Record has 8 or fewer fields and no related records: right-side drawer (the Sheet component in vois-components), view first with an Edit action or edit directly. Record has tabs, a timeline, related records, or a long form: full page, reached from an Open action in the drawer. Only a confirmation: Dialog. The open row id is in the URL and the active row stays highlighted.
nodes.basis_note: decision. Confirmed by Om. Replaces the earlier rule that view-first uses a modal. The 8-field threshold is Claude's proposal.

nodes.condition: A user edits data from a table.
nodes.outcome: One atomic, low-risk value: inline cell edit. Several fields or cross-field validation: the drawer form. The same change on many rows: a bulk bar action or bulk edit page. Irreversible or high-impact: the drawer form plus a confirmation dialog.

nodes.condition: A table has bulk actions.
nodes.outcome: Add a leading checkbox column. The header checkbox is tri-state (none, some, all on this page). Shift-click selects a range. Selected rows get a tint and a checked box, never tint alone. Simple tables have no checkbox column.

nodes.condition: A paginated table has a full page selected and more results exist.
nodes.outcome: Offer a "select all N" control next to the selection count. Say how many rows an action will touch before the user confirms it.

nodes.condition: One or more rows are selected.
nodes.outcome: Show a bar anchored to the table with the selected count, 2 to 3 visible actions with the rest in a DropdownMenu, and a clear-selection control. The destructive action is last and visually distinct. A persistent bar with disabled actions at zero selected is fine when the table is mainly used for bulk work.
nodes.basis_note: observed. Floating bar and persistent bar both appear. The floating bar is the default, judgment.

nodes.condition: A bulk action deletes, archives, or otherwise cannot be undone cheaply.
nodes.outcome: Confirm first and state the count. Use a Dialog (see JOB-CONFIRM-DESTRUCTIVE). If the action can be undone, skip the dialog and offer undo in the confirmation toast instead.

nodes.condition: A column can be sorted.
nodes.outcome: Clicking its header cycles ascending, descending, none. The sorted header shows direction and carries aria-sort. One active sort unless the product genuinely needs more. Sort resets paging to page 1.

nodes.condition: A simple table has one or two filter dimensions.
nodes.outcome: Use a single Filter control that opens a Popover. Applied filters show as dismissible chips under the toolbar. Search sits beside it.

nodes.pattern_name: Filter builder on a complex table
nodes.condition: A complex table has many filterable fields.
nodes.outcome: Use rows of field, operator, value, with Add filter, Apply, and Clear filters. Keep applied filters visible as chips after the builder closes.

nodes.condition: A complex table has more columns than most users need at once.
nodes.outcome: Offer show or hide, reorder, and pin, plus a Reset to default. A column header menu holds per-column actions (sort, move, hide). The first column cannot be hidden.
nodes.basis_note: observed. First column cannot be hidden is judgment.

nodes.condition: A complex table has a density control.
nodes.outcome: Offer Dense, Regular, and Comfortable. Row height and cell padding come from tokens. Simple tables have one density and no toggle. Remember the choice per user.
nodes.basis_note: decision. Set by Om: density toggle on complex tables only.

nodes.condition: Users repeat the same combination of filters, sort, and columns.
nodes.outcome: Offer named views as tabs or a view switcher above the toolbar. A view stores filters, sort, columns, and density. Show an unsaved-changes state when the current setup differs from the saved view.

nodes.condition: A table has search, filters, sort, page, or an open row.
nodes.outcome: Keep each of them in the URL. Reload, back, and a shared link restore the same view, including the open drawer.

nodes.condition: A table has rows users act on repeatedly.
nodes.outcome: Up and Down move row focus. Enter opens the row. Space toggles selection. Esc closes the drawer. Cmd or Ctrl plus Enter saves an edit. Show the shortcut hints where a drawer has them.
nodes.basis_note: observed. Shortcut hints appear in Supabase, Twenty, and Midday drawers.

nodes.pattern_name: Step through rows from the drawer
nodes.condition: A user reviews many rows one after another.
nodes.outcome: Put previous and next controls in the drawer, bound to the Up and Down keys. The table row highlight follows. Stepping past the last row on a page loads the next page.

nodes.condition: A user edits one low-risk value in a cell.
nodes.outcome: Save on commit (Enter or blur) and confirm with a toast that offers Undo. If the save fails, revert the cell, mark the row, and keep the typed value available to retry. Surface the failure as `PATH-TABLE-ERROR-ROW-ACTION` says.

nodes.condition: A user edits several cells or rows, or one value's validity depends on another.
nodes.outcome: Hold edits locally and show an unsaved-changes bar with Save and Discard. Edited cells are visibly marked. Save is blocked while any edit is invalid, with a summary of what to fix. Never drop valid edits because one is invalid. Leaving the page with unsaved edits asks first.

nodes.condition: A cell is editable in place.
nodes.outcome: A single click or Enter on a focused cell enters edit mode. Esc cancels and restores the value. Enter commits. Show the cell's edit state with a visible border, not just a cursor. If the table is a grid with arrow-key cell navigation, use role="grid". Otherwise keep a plain table.

nodes.condition: A table is loading for the first time.
nodes.outcome: Show the real column headers and skeleton rows that match the loaded column widths. Never a full-area spinner.

nodes.condition: A filter, sort, or page change reloads data.
nodes.outcome: Keep the stale rows on screen with a small busy indicator. Do not blank the table.

nodes.condition: The user has never created anything here and can create from this screen.
nodes.outcome: Show an EmptyState with the primary create action. Headers stay visible.

nodes.condition: Search or filters removed every row.
nodes.outcome: Say that filters caused it and offer Clear filters. Use an inline message, not a full EmptyState.

nodes.condition: No rows is a normal, good state, such as no live calls or no open issues.
nodes.outcome: Say so plainly. No call to action.

nodes.condition: The user cannot see any rows because of their role.
nodes.outcome: Say that access is the reason and who can grant it. Do not show the first-use create action.

nodes.condition: A plan limit hides some rows.
nodes.outcome: Put a notice above the table that says so, with the upgrade action. Do not leave it to the footer.

nodes.condition: The table's data request fails.
nodes.outcome: Replace the rows with an inline panel in the table area: the cause when known and a Retry. Toolbar and headers stay, so filters survive. Not a full-screen modal.
nodes.basis_note: observed. A full-screen modal for a single failure is the anti-example (Asana).

nodes.condition: Rows can change state.
nodes.outcome: Support these: default, hover, focus-visible, selected, active (its drawer is open), editing, saving, error, just-added, and disabled or archived. Each has a distinct visual that does not rely on color alone.

nodes.condition: A delete, archive, status change, or similar action on one row fails.
nodes.outcome: If the UI updated optimistically, roll it back. Mark that row with an error state and offer Retry. Surface the failure with whichever component righter's error decision tree picks, anchored to the row where it can be. The row is the anchor for the error, not the page.

nodes.pattern_name: A cell or field is invalid
nodes.condition: An edited cell fails validation.
nodes.outcome: Show the message next to the field. In a drawer form it sits under the field. For a cell it opens in a tooltip or popover. Validate on commit or blur, not on every keystroke. Tint the cell and add an icon. Keep what the user typed.

nodes.pattern_name: A bulk or import operation partly failed
nodes.condition: Some rows in a bulk action or import succeed and some fail.
nodes.outcome: Show an Inline Alert above the table with the counts. It is contextual to the table, so it is not an Alert Banner. Mark failed rows with an icon or count in the row gutter. Offer a "show only rows with errors" toggle and the choice to continue with the rows that are ready. When users cannot fix rows in place, offer an export of the failed rows. Name the real cause on each failure.

nodes.condition: A commit, save, or load fails.
nodes.outcome: Move focus to the first error. Announce errors through an aria-live="polite" region. Never clear the user's data to show an error.

nodes.condition: Rendering any table.
nodes.outcome: Use a real table element with th and scope. Do not rebuild it from div elements. The sortable header is a button inside the th.

nodes.condition: A row opens a detail view when clicked.
nodes.outcome: The first-column value is the real link or button, so keyboard, screen readers, and middle-click work. The row click is an enhancement on top. Clicks on checkboxes, action menus, and links inside the row do not open the drawer.

nodes.condition: A row has sub-rows or a short secondary detail.
nodes.outcome: Use a leading chevron button that toggles aria-expanded. Expanded content stays inside the table. If the detail is a full record, use the drawer instead.

nodes.condition: A table is below the sm container width and stacks its rows (4 or fewer columns, see PATH-B-NARROW).
nodes.outcome: The first column is the row title. Show up to three more values under or beside it: one or two secondary values below the title, one trailing value aligned to the end, and status as a Badge. Nothing is dropped. With 4 or fewer columns every value fits. The whole row is the tap target and opens the record.
nodes.basis_note: observed. Phone apps show lists, not shrunken tables: a title, a subtitle, and a trailing value. The 3-value cap is judgment.

nodes.pattern_name: Row open on a narrow screen
nodes.condition: A row opens its record below the sm container width.
nodes.outcome: The drawer takes the full width and shows a back control instead of a close control. Back and the URL behave as they do on a wide screen. A record with tabs, a timeline, or related records still escalates to a full page.
nodes.basis_note: judgment. Phone apps navigate to a detail screen rather than slide a side panel, and a right-anchored Sheet is full width at this size anyway. Mobbin had no narrow web table to confirm it.

nodes.condition: A narrow list has bulk actions.
nodes.outcome: Selection is a mode. An explicit Select action enters it, and the checkbox column appears only then. The header shows "N selected" with Select all and Cancel. The bulk bar sits at the bottom of the screen with 2 to 4 actions, the destructive one last and in the destructive color. A destructive action confirms with the count before it runs. Leaving the mode clears the selection.
nodes.basis_note: observed. Where a bar shows icons only, labels stay available as accessible names.

nodes.condition: User is showing what a product or business offers to people who are not yet using it: a landing page, homepage, or product marketing page. Not a pricing page (PATH-F) and not product UI.
nodes.outcome: Use the Marketing Page pattern. Every feature block is the same stack: image, short title, one or two sentences, one link. Sections are far apart and text inside them is tight. PATH-G-* rules apply. Words go to righter (slot limits), type and spacing to vois-tokens (DS-MKT). These are taste rules for marketing surfaces, not general laws.

nodes.rule_name: One idea per section
nodes.condition: Any section on a marketing page.
nodes.outcome: One heading, one block of content, one link. If a section needs two headings, it is two sections.

nodes.rule_name: Three blocks max
nodes.condition: Any row or stack of blocks on a marketing page.
nodes.outcome: No more than three blocks. If there are more, group them (five programs become three audience tiles) and link to the detail. Three is a ceiling, not a target. Blocks should still differ in size or emphasis.

nodes.rule_name: Detail goes behind a link
nodes.condition: Full schedules, bios, long FAQs, or any long list on a marketing page.
nodes.outcome: Put the full version on its own page. Show a taste on the page: about 5 schedule rows, one coach sentence, 3 questions, each with a link to the rest.

nodes.rule_name: Image tile first
nodes.condition: A feature block on a marketing page.
nodes.outcome: Large rounded image tile, then a title, then one or two sentences, then one link. Tiles are at least 300px tall on mobile.

nodes.rule_name: No dividers
nodes.condition: Sections on a marketing page that blur together.
nodes.outcome: Do not use hairlines, boxes, or borders to separate sections. Increase the section gap instead (DS-MKT-006).

nodes.rule_name: Left-align by default
nodes.condition: Text and block alignment on a marketing page.
nodes.outcome: Left-align. Center only the closing call to action.

nodes.rule_name: One primary button per view
nodes.condition: Buttons and calls to action on a marketing page.
nodes.outcome: One primary button per view. A secondary button is allowed in the hero only. Repeat the primary call to action at most twice on a page (hero and close). Everything else is a plain link.

nodes.rule_name: Footer at heading scale
nodes.condition: The footer of a marketing page.
nodes.outcome: Repeat the nav as large links at h2 size plus the wordmark. Small print stays small.
